what_it_does: 3D Gaussian Splatting is a technique for representing a real-world scene as a cloud of millions of tiny colored, semi-transparent blobs, enabling photorealistic novel-view synthesis — generating what the scene would look like from a new camera angle. Running it in real time on a phone or headset is extremely demanding because of the sheer number of blobs and the cost of projecting and blending them all at full resolution for every frame. MetaSapiens combines two complementary strategies. The first is efficiency-aware pruning: blobs that contribute little to the final image, or that are costly to process on the target hardware relative to their visual benefit, are removed from the model during a preparation step, shrinking the total computation. The second is foveated rendering: human eyes perceive fine detail only in the small central region where gaze is directed, while peripheral vision is much blurrier; MetaSapiens exploits this by rendering the center of the frame at full quality and the surrounding area at lower quality or with fewer blobs, dramatically reducing the total number of blob-blending operations. The two techniques are designed together with the mobile chip's execution model to maximize frames per second.
